narrativeProgression.description: Margaret Johnston introduces herself and expresses gratitude for the forum.
She mentions her previous experience with similar forums and highlights the importance of addressing poverty issues.
She emphasizes the NDP's commitment to making life more affordable for families.
She shares her observations from the roundtable discussions, noting the prevalence of health-related issues.
She outlines some of the NDP's proposed solutions, including increased healthcare funding, shorter wait times, and new family health clinics.
She further elaborates on the NDP's plans to support families caring for the ill, attract doctors to underserved communities, and forgive student debt for medical professionals.
She criticizes her Liberal opponent for failing to address poverty issues during her time in office and argues that the NDP can be trusted to deliver on their promises.
She concludes her speech by asking for the audience's support in the upcoming election.

youtube_description: Margaret Johnson, Candidate for the Ontario NDP in Kitchener Centre riding, responding  to the table discussions on social issues and poverty. The all-candidates session was hosted by the Social Planning Council of KW and Poverty Free KW Action Group on May 28 at YWCA Mary's Place Community Room. See the discussion notes, fact sheets on social issues, party platform analysis through the local community Framework on Poverty Elimination on www.waterlooregion.org/ontario-election-2014.
